title: Grieving family wants to know why man was shot by P.A. police
subtitle: The potential witness was driving a Ford Focus in the area of Prince Albert where the shooting occurred.
article: Rhonda Gardiner says she just wants to know why her son John was shot and killed by Prince Albert police in January.
"Why did they shoot him like that?" she asked in an interview on Friday.
Family members spoke with the StarPhoenix about their lingering questions.

John died on the night of Jan. 16 after a Prince Albert police officer shot him in the 400 block of South Industrial Drive. His death is now under investigation by the Saskatchewan Serious Incident Response Team, the independent, civilian-led team created to investigate all serious incidents involving police, including when an officer seriously injures or kills someone during an altercation.
In a previous media release, Prince Albert city police said an officer driving a marked police vehicle started an investigation on that block at 10:40 p.m. on Jan. 16.

"During the course of the encounter, a short foot pursuit ensued, and a confrontation occurred during which one member of the PAPS discharged their service pistol, striking a 34-year-old man," SIRT said in a media release.
According to SIRT, Prince Albert police officers provided first aid until paramedics arrived and took the man to hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.
Police notified SIRT and the independent body's civilian executive director launched an investigation.
Family members say John was a genuine, outgoing and protective person.
He liked outdoor activities, quadding, fishing and had been working in the mines until he was laid off in October and had been looking for work, his cousin Lisa Corrigal said.

John was younger than her, so she was like an auntie to him and he had been living at her home, Lisa said. John was a member of Canoe Lake First Nation, grew up in Buffalo Narrows and Ile-a-la-Crosse, and was raised by his late grandparents.
"He loved his mom so much and he let the world know that all the time," Lisa said.
When she learned John died, she didn't know what to think and didn't have any details, but she heard he was shot and wanted to know why someone would shoot him, she said.
When she read media reports about a police-involved shooting, it left her in shock, she said.
"All we knew basically was what the press was saying."

John's next of kin, his former girlfriend, was told about his death and shared the news with his family. Lisa said she didn't have any contact from police and decided to try to find out what had happened on the night of the shooting.
Lisa said she and her sister, Jasmyne Gardiner-Bird, John's cousin and best friend, had received messages from him asking if they could send money to help him pay for gas.
She spoke to the woman who was with him and witnessed what happened, she said.
"All I know, all I'm going to say is he didn't deserve to die. They didn't have to pull out the gun because they weren't being threatened in any way."
Lisa said she was told two police officers were questioning John and the woman and one officer called him "Johnson."

She was told the officer had told John they were going to arrest him and he said "not tonight" because he had something to do tomorrow, but would turn himself in, she said. She was told the officer then reached for handcuffs and John started running with an officer chasing him. Then shots were fired.
"He just had a backpack and he ran and he got shot. Why? I just want to know why," she said.
The Federation of Sovereign Indigenous Nations' justice secretariat is investigating and the FSIN has been supporting the family.

SIRT issued a request for a potential witness to come forward after investigators reviewed surveillance video recovered from the area of the shooting. SIRT has since located the individual sought, but had no further comment Friday. It has said it will release a final report to the public within 90 days of the conclusion of the investigation.
As they grieve, family members have also been dealing with speculation on social media, including people commenting that John "deserved" to be shot.

Lisa said she reviewed media reports and the statement issued by police, but saw nothing that would lead people to assume John was armed. The SIRT and Prince Albert police media releases have made no statements indicating he had a weapon.
People have just made assumptions, Lisa said.
She said she wants to know why police drew a gun instead of a Taser or pepper spray.
"I'm not going to stop until I find out."
